description: Cedar Shift is a multidisciplinary team exploring how SPHEREx observations can reveal changes in the infrared sky. We combine real NASA data, rigorous science, intuitive visualization, and compelling storytelling to make moving and changing celestial objects accessible to everyone. We welcome expertise in astronomy, scientific Python, web development, UI/UX, data visualization, and science communication.
summary:
Cedar Shift transforms NASA SPHEREx observations into an intuitive public experience for exploring how the infrared sky changes over time. SPHEREx observes the entire sky across 102 near-infrared spectral channels, creating an extraordinary dataset in which asteroids, comets, nearby stars, brown dwarfs, and other objects can reveal themselves through motion or variability.

Cedar Shift makes these changes easier to explore by allowing users to select a region of the sky or a featured target and compare observations from different epochs through an interactive web interface. Instead of requiring users to manipulate large astronomical FITS datasets themselves, the platform turns real SPHEREx observations into accessible visual comparisons while preserving their scientific context.

Our objective is not to claim the discovery of Planet X, but to lower the barrier between professional astronomical datasets and the public, giving anyone a simple way to explore a changing infrared universe.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

Cedar Shift addresses a fundamental usability problem in modern astronomy: enormous scientific datasets contain meaningful changes, but inspecting them normally requires specialist tools and knowledge.

Our project transforms real NASA SPHEREx observations into an accessible web experience designed for both curious members of the public and technically interested users. Users can explore a sky position or selected astronomical target and compare observations obtained at different times, making positional motion and other changes easier to recognize visually.

The project uses SPHEREx data made publicly available through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). Astronomical data are retrieved and processed using scientific Python tools such as Astropy and Astroquery, with the resulting information presented through an interactive web interface.

Rather than attempting to transfer the enormous SPHEREx archive directly into a browser, Cedar Shift focuses on the requested region of the sky and processes only the data required for that view. This provides a practical path toward an experience that is responsive, scalable, and capable of incorporating future SPHEREx releases.

The creative core of Cedar Shift is the modernization of the astronomical “blink comparator”: observations of the same sky are compared across time so objects that move or change become easier to notice. We combine that concept with modern interactive visualization and the unique spectral richness of SPHEREx.

The intended impact is both scientific and educational: make NASA astrophysics data more accessible, help users understand how astronomers identify changes in the sky, and create a foundation upon which future citizen-science functionality could enable large numbers of people to participate in exploring SPHEREx observations.

Cedar Shift does not claim that visually identified changes represent new planets or confirmed discoveries. Potential changes require additional observations and scientific validation.
